children: Charoen Pokphand Foods' earnings are likely to recover strongly in 2H, says Yupapan Polpornprasert of ttb wealth securities in a report. Drivers are higher livestock prices, resilient demand, and manageable feed costs, the analyst says. Thailand's swine prices rebounded to 72 baht per kilogram in August from 63 baht per kilogram in 2Q, with supply expected to be constrained for another six to nine months, supporting near-term swine prices. With the farming business accounting for 54% of total revenue, the agro-industrial and food conglomerate has high earnings sensitivity to the livestock cycle, making improving meat prices a key catalyst for the share price. The brokerage raises the stock's target price to 28.00 baht from 23.00 baht with an unchanged buy rating. Shares are 1.3% lower at THB23.40. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
